regime_context: The detector shows a broad, rotation-dominant leadership structure in Canada/TSX with Oil & Gas Producers as the clear leader (score 1.768) but 'one_narrative' false — no single theme is absorbing the tape. The only validated edge on this market is drawdown control via the absolute-trend gate (9 of 16 themes eligible), so the signal supports staying-power discipline, not return forecasting. Rank-IC on this clean sector universe is weak/insignificant, so the momentum ranks are a focus lens only.
emerging_watch: Watching for a CONFIRMED leadership handoff from Oil & Gas to Base Metals & Copper: observing whether XBM.TO closes a full week above XEG.TO on a relative basis while both remain trend-gate eligible. The watch retires if Oil & Gas re-extends its lead (margin > 0.5) before any such handoff week completes.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: XEG.TO holds the top rank and is eligible (absolute-trend gate), with the highest durability_bar (0.62) and healthy breadth (0.643) — the only leading theme with both leader rank and solid participation. Crowding_z at 1.01 flags it as crowded, which the guardrails cap as a SIZE-DOWN caution, not a fade. The lean rests on the trend-gate (staying power) and breadth/dur-quality, not on the momentum score itself.
evidence: crowding_z=1.01 -> crowded=true, a sizing caution only
theses.dissent: Crowding has no basket-level forward edge and the theme's hurst_tag is 'mixed' — trend persistence is not clean — so a crowding unwind could punish late-cyclical energy exposure quickly.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its 50-day average for 5 consecutive sessions before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: XBM.TO is eligible with the second-highest score (1.545) and is the designated rotation.challenger. It has a non-crowded crowding_z (0.89) and moderate breadth (0.556), but its hurst_tag is 'mean-revert' — meaning short-term reversal risk is high. The lean is supported by the trend-gate eligibility and challenger status, but tempered by the mean-revert texture, which argues against momentum chasing.
theses.dissent: The 'mean-revert' hurst tag directly contradicts a trend-following lean — base metals may already be overextended and prone to snap back.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO gives back 3% relative to the S&P/TSX benchmark over the next 10 trading days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
